page: Microsoft Azure L4aos_v4 is a virtual machine instance belonging to the Laosv4 family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with an x86_64 architecture, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with multithreading. The CPU operates at a clock speed of 3.7 GHz and includes 32 MB of L3 cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 KB of L1d cache. It supports advanced instruction sets including AVX-512, AES cryptography, and SHA extensions.

This instance is equipped with 32.0 GB of system memory, yielding a memory-to-core ratio of 8.0 GB per core. For local storage, it bundles a substantial 2880 GB NVMe SSD, which is Premium Storage capable. No GPU accelerators are present on this instance, and it does not include complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Performance benchmarks show strong single-core capabilities, with stress-ng single-core CPU and Geekbench single-core scores placing in the top 25 percent. However, multi-core performance and memory bandwidth present notable tradeoffs. While write memory bandwidth and Redis SET operations perform at average levels, read-only memory bandwidth and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression fall into the bottom 25 percent. Similarly, database operations and static web serving throughput are relatively weak, indicating potential bottlenecks in high-concurrency read-heavy workloads.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the L4aos_v4 offers a dense combination of high-capacity local NVMe storage and memory relative to its 4 vCPU count. This makes it a strong candidate for workloads that require fast local scratch space or moderate memory footprints without needing massive parallel compute. Recommended workloads include localized database hosting, text processing, single-threaded data manipulation, and lightweight LLM inference using small models.
description: The Microsoft Azure L4aos_v4 is a virtual machine instance powered by a 3.7 GHz AMD EPYC 9V74 processor with 4 dedicated vCPUs and 32.0 GB of RAM. It features a substantial 2880 GB local NVMe SSD, making it highly capable for storage-intensive tasks, though it lacks dedicated GPU hardware. Benchmark data reveals strong single-core CPU and text processing performance, alongside average multi-core and write memory bandwidth capabilities. However, it exhibits weaker read-only memory bandwidth and database operation speeds. Qualitatively, the L4aos_v4 provides a resource-dense profile for workloads requiring significant local storage and memory relative to compute power. It is well-suited for localized databases, text processing, and moderate memory-bound applications.
